design_notes.what_this_feature_is: The fourth feature of phase 013 (third of the parallel group {094,095,096}): ships a governed, frontmattered consumer template, templates/DoD.md, that projects standard/definition_of_done.md onto a fillable per-project checklist -- one checklist block per Step/Handoff/Gate/Feature/Plan/Merge/Release layer citing the standard's own Section N, a {{PROJECT_SPECIFIC_DONE_CRITERIA}} extension block, a floor-not-guarantee closing note citing the standard's Section 12, and a dod_ref pointer note -- registered in NIZAM.json (both the templates[] top-level array and modules[path=="templates"].key_documents) and templates/README.md (new row, description-count edit, version bump, first change_log block).
design_notes.verify_c1_templates_governed: VERIFIED (not assumed), corrected for check-set precision (a prior revision round conflated two different validator invocation modes' check sets as though interchangeable): tools/validate.sh's build_shipped_md_set() (tools/validate.sh, function starting the line after the 'Shared file-set builder' banner) iterates `for d in standard methodology registry templates` and recursively finds every `*.md` under each, so templates/DoD.md IS a member of the shipped-doc set the moment it exists on disk. In DEFAULT mode (tools/validate.sh:2500-2507) and in --payload mode (tools/validate.sh:2478-2485, since build_payload_md_set() likewise includes `templates` in its payload-mode module list), that shipped/payload-set membership routes templates/DoD.md through check_c1_frontmatter_schema, check_c2_format, check_c3_fences, check_c5_branding, and check_c8_version_changelog -- i.e. C1/C2/C3/C5/C8 -- run as part of the whole-set array, not singled out per-file. In --target mode (tools/validate.sh:2449-2458), a `*.md` target is instead routed to a DIFFERENT five-check set run individually against just that one file: check_c1_frontmatter_schema, check_c2_format, check_c3_fences, check_c9_path_resolution, check_c10_consistency -- i.e. C1/C2/C3/C9/C10 -- which is the set this contract's verification item 2 (`bash tools/validate.sh --target templates/DoD.md`) actually exercises and per-check asserts. templates/DoD.md is therefore governed exactly like templates/AGENTS.md and templates/CONTEXT.md under BOTH invocation shapes, not exempt under either -- but the two shapes check a DIFFERENT five-check set (C1/C2/C3/C5/C8 vs. C1/C2/C3/C9/C10), and this contract's verification distinguishes them rather than treating the two as the same set under two names. Consequence: the six required frontmatter keys (standard/NDS.md Sec 2) are not optional for this file -- C1 will FAIL without them under either invocation.
design_notes.verify_enumeration_guard_scope: VERIFIED (not assumed) -- REFUTES the plan's premise that the disk-to-index enumeration guard already sweeps templates/: tools/fixtures_self_test.sh's `_f055_real_tree` function (the actual NDEBT-005 disk-to-index mechanization, distinct from build_shipped_md_set) runs `for m in standard methodology registry ecosystem` and calls `vlib_enumeration_complete NIZAM.json "${m}" "${m}" '*.md'` only for those four module keys. `templates` is NOT a member of that loop today, and this contract's non_goals explicitly forbid editing tools/fixtures_self_test.sh (out of scope; that file belongs to no phase-013 feature). Consequence, recorded honestly rather than overclaimed: `bash tools/fixtures_self_test.sh` passing after this feature lands is a REQUIRED regression guard (nothing else must break) but it does NOT itself prove templates/DoD.md's registration completeness in NIZAM.json, unlike feature 093's identical-looking acceptance test against the standard/ module, which the real-tree loop DOES cover. The actual registration proof for this feature is verification item 3 below (the direct python membership+count assertion against both NIZAM.json sites), which is why that assertion is load-bearing rather than a redundant restatement of the self-test.

frontmatter_pin.no_change_log_key: DECISION: templates/DoD.md carries ONLY the six required NDS.md Sec 2 keys, with NO change_log block -- mirroring the verified precedent of all four existing templates/*.md files (AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, DEBT.md, ADR_TEMPLATE.md), none of which carries a change_log key, in contrast to standard/definition_of_done.md (a Tier-1 standard document, contract 093), which does. change_log is optional per NDS.md Sec 2.1 and the template-family precedent is to omit it; this also means C8 (version-bump-vs-changelog) never applies to this file after this feature lands, since C8 skips files that are new at HEAD and this file's version will not change again within this contract's scope.

design_notes.ecosystem_layer_decision: DECISION: the template ships SEVEN full checklist blocks -- Step-Done, Handoff-Done, Gate-Done, Feature-Done, Plan-Done, Merge-Done, Release-Done (standard/definition_of_done.md Sections 3-9) -- and does NOT ship an eighth full Ecosystem-Done checklist block. PROVENANCE CORRECTION (this field previously fabricated a plan quotation -- 'decide whether ecosystem belongs for a single consumer repo and record the decision' -- attributing to F-095 plan prose a question that was in fact posed by the orchestrator's proposal brief to the contract generator, not by the plan itself; corrected here): the seven-block-plus-Section-10-pointer design is an orchestrator-directed design decision, and the plan of record (definition-of-done-stateful-kettle.md F-095) has since been updated to record it directly. The plan's own current text reads, verbatim: 'orchestrator-directed design decision (2026-08-19, recorded here as the plan of record; original brief posed the question to the proposal generator)'. Rationale (real, not fabricated): a default single-consumer-repo template must not presume multi-repository ecosystem participation -- Ecosystem-Done (Section 10) governs multi-repository engineering claims closed with path-referenced closure evidence against a shared ecosystem scope document, a topology most copies of this template will not have; this is the identical reasoning underlying NDEBT-001's deliberate stance (docs/planning/DEBT.md), under which this very framework repository is itself kept OUTSIDE ECOSYSTEM.json scope by explicit human resolution recorded 2026-07-07 ('the repository is deliberately kept OUTSIDE the NizamIQ ecosystem scope as a generalised framework. It will not be registered in ECOSYSTEM.json'). Instead the template carries one short, non-checklist pointer paragraph directly beneath the Release-Done block, naming standard/definition_of_done.md Section 10 by citation and stating in prose (no checkboxes) that a project which IS an ecosystem participant should additionally track Ecosystem-Done there -- so the citation is honest and complete (all eight standard layers are named somewhere in the template) without manufacturing seven-going-on-eight checklist items a majority of consumers would leave permanently unchecked.
design_notes.dod_ref_pointer_decision: DECISION on the 094-landing-order question: this template's pointer note is written to be true regardless of whether feature 094 has landed at the moment a consumer copies this file, using BOTH allowed forms together for redundancy and honesty -- (1) it names feature 094 generically, by feature id and phase ('an optional dod_ref key added to several Nizam schemas by phase 013, feature 094'), never asserting present-tense that the key already exists on any specific schema at the reader's checkout; and (2) it describes the mechanism generically ('if your artifact's governing schema carries an optional dod_ref string property, set it to this file's project-specific copy's path to bind that artifact's completion claim to this checklist'). Path tokens used in this note (e.g. schema/contract.schema.json, schema/qa_verdict.schema.json as illustrative examples) are safe under check C9's path-token extractor regardless of 094's landing order, because those schema FILES already exist on disk today (094 only adds an optional KEY inside them, which C9's path-resolution check cannot observe or depend on) -- independently confirmed today via `ls schema/*.schema.json`. No non-existent path is ever named.
design_notes.body_layer_citations: Verified against the real, currently-shipped standard/definition_of_done.md (feature 093, landed): Section 3 = Step-Done, Section 4 = Handoff-Done, Section 5 = Gate-Done, Section 6 = Feature-Done, Section 7 = Plan-Done, Section 8 = Merge-Done, Section 9 = Release-Done, Section 10 = Ecosystem-Done, Section 12 = 'A Floor, Not a Guarantee'. Every per-layer checklist block's citation line must read '(standard/definition_of_done.md Section N)' with the exact N pinned above -- an off-by-one citation (e.g. citing Section 5 for Feature-Done) would be a factual error this contract's verification checks for individually, not just an aggregate grep for the file path.
design_notes.placeholder_and_style_pins: Every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` token in the body appears strictly below the closing frontmatter `---` line, mirroring the AGENTS.md/CONTEXT.md/DEBT.md/ADR_TEMPLATE.md precedent (none of the four carries a placeholder above its own closing `---`). At least 5 distinct `{{...}}` occurrences (feature-095 acceptance test 3, `grep -c '{{' templates/DoD.md` >= 5): {{PROJECT}} in the header, {{PROJECT_SPECIFIC_DONE_CRITERIA}} as its own block, plus at minimum three more (e.g. {{REPO_NAME}} or per-block {{OWNER}}/{{DATE}} fill-ins at the generator's discretion) -- the generator MAY add more than the floor of 5 but must not fall below it. Every fenced code block, if any are used (e.g. for a machine-readable checklist excerpt), declares a language tag (mechanically enforced by C3). Every repository-relative, directory-qualified path cited in the body (standard/definition_of_done.md and any illustrative schema/*.schema.json examples) must resolve on disk at the commit this feature lands, mechanically enforced by C9 in both --target and default-sweep modes. House citation style: backticked paths + 'Section N' prose, never markdown link syntax `[text](path)`, matching the verified zero-markdown-link convention already established by contract 093's hard_style_rules for standard/definition_of_done.md and independently re-confirmed today by inspection of templates/AGENTS.md and templates/CONTEXT.md, neither of which contains a markdown link in body text.

verification.acceptance_test: Each of the seven per-layer checklist blocks cites the pinned Section N (body_layer_citations above) for standard/definition_of_done.md, proving the citations are individually correct rather than merely present somewhere in the file. Anchored on the layer's own markdown HEADING line (a heading line naming the layer, e.g. '## Step-Done'), with the citation required to appear before the NEXT heading line -- not on first free-text occurrence of the layer name plus an arbitrary fixed-width window, which could false-positive on an unrelated mention (e.g. inside the dod_ref pointer note or a table of contents) preceding the real block.
verification.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
text = open('templates/DoD.md').read()
pairs = {
    'Step-Done': 'Section 3',
    'Handoff-Done': 'Section 4',
    'Gate-Done': 'Section 5',
    'Feature-Done': 'Section 6',
    'Plan-Done': 'Section 7',
    'Merge-Done': 'Section 8',
    'Release-Done': 'Section 9',
}
missing = []
for layer, section in pairs.items():
    heading_re = re.compile(r'^#{1,6}\s.*\b' + re.escape(layer) + r'\b', re.MULTILINE)
    m = heading_re.search(text)
    if not m:
        missing.append(f'{layer}: no heading line found naming this layer')
        continue
    start = m.end()
    next_heading = re.search(r'\n#{1,6}\s', text[start:])
    end = start + next_heading.start() if next_heading else len(text)
    block = text[start:end]
    if 'standard/definition_of_done.md' not in block or section not in block:
        missing.append(f'{layer}: citation to standard/definition_of_done.md {section} not found before its block\'s next heading')
assert not missing, missing
idx12 = text.index('Section 12')
window12 = text[max(0, idx12 - 200): idx12 + 200]
assert 'standard/definition_of_done.md' in window12, 'floor-not-guarantee note must cite Section 12'
print('PASS all seven layer blocks cite their pinned Section N (heading-anchored); Section 12 floor-note present')
PY
